card.title: How To Fix an iPhone 7 With No Image, Turns On But No Display

source.title: How To Fix an iPhone 7 With No Image, Turns On But No Display

claims.statement: Confirm a board fault with a known-good screen, about 1 A USB charge, sounds/vibration, a flashlight check for the logo and checking it is not in DFU mode.
Diode-check LCD connector J4502: good lines read about 200–700 mV; common shorts are PP5V7_LCM_AVDDH_CONN, PP5V7_MESON_AVDDH_CONN and PN5V7_LCM_MESON_AVDDN_CONN.
Inject only about 2–3 V (never above 5.7 V) to find those shorts so heat stays localised.
OL on PP1V8_LCM_CONN usually means a damaged filter FL3906 (both sides should read the same).
If connector readings are fine, check Chestnut U3703 (image power IC): C3703 must not have continuity across it; look for corrosion under U3703 and replace it.

procedure: Rule out screen, DFU and backlight-only faults.
Inject 2–3 V into shorted LCM lines to find the cap.
Check FL3906 if PP1V8_LCM_CONN is OL.
Check C3703 and corrosion under U3703; replace U3703.
card.caveats: Community-written Repair Wiki page, paraphrased; check the linked page (and its images) before acting on a reading.
